invariants.statement: A promo code can only be redeemed once per account

sequence: POST /api/v1/subscriptions/upgrade {plan:pro, promo_code:SAVE50} as Account_A — expect 200 with discounted price
POST /api/v1/subscriptions/upgrade {plan:enterprise, promo_code:SAVE50} as Account_A — expect 400 promo already redeemed
Check invoice amount for second upgrade to confirm discount was not applied
preconditions: Account_A has not previously used SAVE50
Account_A is on a plan eligible for upgrade
tests.oracle: Second upgrade invoice amount equals full price (no discount applied)

sequence: Fire two simultaneous POST /api/v1/subscriptions/upgrade requests with promo_code:SAVE50 from Account_A
Check both response invoice amounts — if both show discounted price the race won
preconditions: Account_A has not previously used SAVE50
Two concurrent sessions available for Account_A
tests.oracle: Both responses return discounted invoice amount (50% off applied twice total)

invariants.statement: Downgrade is blocked for 30 days after an upgrade

sequence: Immediately POST /api/v1/subscriptions/downgrade {plan:basic} — expect 400 or 403 with lockout message
If 200 returned, GET /api/v1/subscriptions — confirm plan is basic and billing cycle restarted
preconditions: Account_A is on basic plan before test
tests.oracle: Downgrade POST returns 200 and account plan changes to basic within seconds of upgrade

untestable.invariant: Billing charge is accurate to the cent
untestable.reason: Requires payment processor integration; sandbox environment may not charge real amounts

summary: Account_A can redeem promo code SAVE50 twice via a race condition in the upgrade endpoint, achieving 50% discount on two billing cycles
